title: Third-Party Audit Access: Which Companies Allow External Safety Audits and What Do Auditors Find?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: establishing whether access level predicts audit findings directly informs governance design around mandatory audit access requirements.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: surveying documented audits across multiple years and coding access levels requires careful research skills manageable with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: surveying all documented third-party AI safety audits from 2022-2025 is a broad data collection exercise with unclear boundaries.

novelty.reasoning: The frontier AI auditing literature discusses access barriers and the FLI Safety Index tracks some audit metrics. However, a comprehensive survey cataloguing all documented third-party audits, coding access levels, and correlating access with finding severity has not been done systematically. The specific access-level-to-findings correlation is partially novel.

evidence: arXiv:2601.11699 'Frontier AI Auditing' (Jan 2026) discusses third-party assessment practices extensively, finding most rely on public info with bespoke contracts limiting transparency
FLI AI Safety Index assesses whether companies commission independent verification, including reviewer identity, independence, scope, depth of access
Transparency scores rose from 37% (2023) to 58% (2024) per Stanford AI Index, but >40% of releases still lack safety information
No comprehensive survey cataloguing all documented third-party AI safety audits with access level coding and finding analysis
